name: pv-migrate
description: CLI tool and kubectl plugin that moves the contents of a Kubernetes PersistentVolumeClaim: directly to another PVC with rsync over SSH, or to and from bucket storage (S3-compatible, Azure Blob, GCS, any rclone remote) with rclone. It runs the data mover inside the cluster as a Job rendered from an embedded Helm chart, and owns no state of its own.

know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer builds infrastructure software professionally. The tool follows least privilege: it needs only the RBAC of the resources it creates, the data mover containers run as a dedicated non-root user where the volume allows it, and the CLI image is built from scratch with no shell. Every transfer uses a fresh SSH key pair that is thrown away with the release. User-supplied paths are checked to stay inside the volume before anything touches the cluster. Every value that reaches the data mover command is quoted as one shell word. Written up in https://github.com/utkuozdemir/pv-migrate/blob/main/docs/security-model.md
know_common_errors_justification: The relevant error classes for this software, and what is done about them. Shell injection through the data mover command: every path, host and remote spec is quoted as a single shell word, and a value the chart cannot carry is rejected with the flag name. Path traversal through `--source-path` and `--dest-path`: resolved against the mount point and rejected when they leave it. Credentials in process arguments: bucket credentials go to the cluster as a Kubernetes Secret, never into the command line. Untrusted parser input from the data movers' logs: the progress parsers are fuzzed. Supply chain: actions pinned by commit, images pinned by digest, signed releases.
crypto_published_justification: The only cryptography is standard: an Ed25519 (or optionally RSA) SSH key pair generated per transfer, SSH for the rsync connection, and TLS for the Kubernetes API and for object storage. All of it comes from Go's standard library, `golang.org/x/crypto`, OpenSSH and rclone.
crypto_call_justification: The project implements no cryptography. Key generation uses `crypto/ed25519`, `crypto/rsa` and `crypto/rand` from Go, and `golang.org/x/crypto/ssh` for the SSH wire formats. The SSH connection itself is OpenSSH inside the data mover containers. TLS comes from client-go and rclone.
crypto_floss_justification: Go standard library, `golang.org/x/crypto`, OpenSSH and rclone. All FLOSS.
crypto_keylength_justification: The default SSH key is Ed25519. The RSA option generates 2048-bit keys. TLS follows Go's defaults on the client side (client-go) and rclone's on the bucket side.
crypto_working_justification: Ed25519 by default, RSA 2048 as an option, OpenSSH and TLS defaults. No broken algorithms in there.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Ed25519 and the OpenSSH and Go TLS defaults.
crypto_pfs_justification: SSH key exchange in OpenSSH is ephemeral by design. Go's TLS uses ECDHE key exchange by default, and always on TLS 1.3.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The tool stores no passwords. Bucket credentials are handed to the cluster as a Kubernetes Secret for the duration of the job and removed with the release.
crypto_random_justification: Go's `crypto/rand` for the SSH key pair.
delivery_mitm_justification: All downloads go over https. Additionally, the checksums file of every release carries a keyless cosign signature, and every container image is signed keyless with cosign: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/pv-migrate/blob/main/docs/install.md#verifying-what-you-downloaded
delivery_unsigned_justification: The checksums file is served over https and has a cosign signature bundle next to it (`checksums.txt.sigstore.json`).

dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Every fuzz target asserts a property, not just the absence of a panic: a parsed progress update is within bounds, a generated config round-trips, a resolved bucket path stays inside its volume. The integration suite runs with `-race`.

coding_standards_justification: gofmt, gofumpt and golangci-lint with all linters, shfmt for shell, helm lint for the embedded chart. The contribution guide says so: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/pv-migrate/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

build_standard_variables_justification: The Go toolchain honors `GOFLAGS`. There is no C compiler involved, the build is `CGO_ENABLED=0`.
build_preserve_debug_justification: `go build` from source keeps the debug information. Only the release binaries are stripped to keep the downloads small.
build_non_recursive_justification: One Go module, one build graph. `go build ./...` resolves the dependencies itself.
build_repeatable_justification: The release builds use `-trimpath`, and the commit time is the timestamp of the binaries and of every archive entry, so the same commit yields the same bytes. The toolchain and every module version are pinned in `go.mod` and `go.sum`, and the goreleaser version in the repo. A CI workflow builds the release files on two different runners and fails if a checksum differs, and the release workflow rebuilds the files on a second runner after publishing and compares them with the published checksums. Both rebuild without the Go cache. The archive entries carry a fixed owner and mode, because an archive entry otherwise records the builder's uid, user name and umask. The data mover images install packages from the Alpine repositories at build time and are not reproducible. Releases before this change were not reproducible. https://github.com/utkuozdemir/pv-migrate/issues/462
installation_common_justification: Homebrew tap, Scoop bucket, krew plugin, release archives per platform, and a container image: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/pv-migrate/blob/main/docs/install.md
installation_standard_variables_justific: The archives are a single binary you put where you want. Homebrew, Scoop and krew place it where those tools place everything. `go install` honors `GOBIN` and `GOPATH`.
installation_development_quick_justifica: `git clone`, `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`. The linters run in containers via `task lint`, at the versions CI uses. A cluster is needed only for the integration suites: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/pv-migrate/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
dependency_monitoring_justification: Renovate updates dependencies continuously, and GitHub Dependabot alerts are enabled for the repository.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Go modules, nothing vendored. A dependency is updated by bumping it in `go.mod`, which Renovate does on its own. The data mover images take rsync, OpenSSH and rclone from the Alpine repositories.
interfaces_current_justification: staticcheck, part of the golangci-lint set, flags deprecated APIs, and the build fails on it.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: On every push and pull request. The result is the check on the commit: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/pv-migrate/blob/main/.github/workflows/build.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: Bug fixes come with a test that would have caught them. For the data mover command and progress parsing bugs that is usually a table case or a fuzz seed, which every test run then replays.
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Unit test statement coverage is 51% over the whole module (`go test -coverpkg=./... ./...`, measured 2026-09-02), and the integration suites alone measure 58% on Codecov. The merged figure of all three suites is what Codecov reports for the `main` branch, and it is below 80%: https://codecov.io/gh/utkuozdemir/pv-migrate
implement_secure_design_justification: Least privilege, fail safe, small attack surface, one-shot keys, quoted commands, checked paths. How each one is applied and checked: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/pv-migrate/blob/main/docs/security-model.md
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The SSH key algorithm is a flag (`--ssh-key-algorithm`, Ed25519 or RSA). The SSH ciphers are OpenSSH's, configurable through the sshd config in the image. TLS parameters follow client-go and rclone.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The SSH key pair is generated per transfer and exists only for it. Bucket credentials arrive through flags or environment variables and are handed to the cluster as a Kubernetes Secret, so they can be rotated on the storage side at any time. Nothing is baked in.
crypto_used_network_justification: The rsync transfer goes over SSH. Talking to the Kubernetes API and to object storage goes over TLS, through client-go and rclone. The one exception is the `mount` strategy, which copies inside a single pod and uses no network at all.
crypto_tls12_justification: The TLS connections are made by client-go and rclone, both of which default to TLS 1.2 as the minimum. The project has no TLS server of its own.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: client-go verifies the API server certificate against the kubeconfig's CA, and rclone verifies the object storage certificate against the system roots. The CLI image ships a CA bundle for that.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: Both TLS clients verify before sending anything. The SSH connection is bootstrapped with a fresh key pair whose public key is placed on the other side by the same tool in the same run.
signed_releases_justification: The checksums file of every release carries a keyless cosign signature bundle, which covers every binary and archive. The four container images are signed keyless with cosign, so there is no stored signing key anywhere. Every release file and image additionally carries a GitHub build provenance attestation. How to verify: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/pv-migrate/blob/main/docs/install.md#verifying-what-you-downloaded. Honest limits: the auto-generated GitHub source archives are not covered, and releases before this change are unsigned.
version_tags_signed_justification: Release tags are signed from the next release on: the release task creates a signed tag from the tip of main, and the release workflow refuses a tag GitHub does not show as verified, or that does not point at the commit being built. Release tags are immutable by ruleset. Tags before that are unsigned.
input_validation_justification: Flags are validated before anything touches the cluster. User-supplied paths are resolved against the volume mount point and rejected when they leave it. Every value interpolated into the data mover command is quoted as one shell word, and a value the chart cannot carry is rejected with the flag name. The operation identifier is validated for length and character set. The progress parsers refuse an update that is out of bounds. All of the parser-shaped code is fuzzed.
hardening_justification: Static binary with no cgo. The CLI image is built from scratch, with no shell. The data mover containers run as a dedicated non-root user when `--non-root` is set, and the chart lets network policies be enabled per component. Each transfer uses a fresh SSH key pair that is removed with the release.
assurance_case_justification: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/pv-migrate/blob/main/docs/security-model.md: security requirements, trust boundaries, threats with their mitigations, and how each is checked.
